name: Shiphrah and Puah, the midwives
charge: Fearing God and not doing as the king of Egypt commanded them
summary: Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill every son at the birthstool. They feared God more than the king and saved the men children alive. God dealt well with them, and because they feared God, he made them houses.
offense: They were given a direct order by the head of state, backed by his power to kill them: when ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, if it be a son, then ye shall kill him (Exodus 1:16). They disobeyed it, and the text states the reason without embellishment: but the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive (Exodus 1:17). That is the rule the apostles afterwards stood on, we ought to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29), and the standard Proverbs sets, if thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; if thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it (Proverbs 24:11-12). Called to account, they answered that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them (Exodus 1:19), which is a statement about the daughters of Israel and not about the nations, and the record neither corrects it nor rebukes them for it.
judgment: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty (Exodus 1:20), and the reason is given again so that it cannot be mistaken for reward of policy: and it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses (Exodus 1:21). Two women at the bottom of an empire were given households of their own, which is the currency this account values, and the increase they had risked their lives to protect is recorded in the same breath. The whole nation that came out of Egypt came through the hands they refused to use. Their names are written and the Pharaoh who commanded them is not, which is itself the verdict.

verses.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.
Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
Praise ye the Lord. Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord, that delighteth greatly in his commandments.
His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed.
Wealth and riches shall be in his house: and his righteousness endureth for ever.

entries.commentary: All the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls, for Joseph was in Egypt already; and Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty, and the land was filled with them. Israel had those babies; the nation did not cast away its children, and the increase was the blessing.

Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph: this is not merely one king but a new kingdom arising, the eighteenth dynasty. Come on, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply and join our enemies: the same wise dealing works on Israel in America today, through movements set up to redirect the people, through Planned Parenthood, and through the prison industrial complex; but the enemy did not count on Christ returning, restoring the nation, and bringing us back to the commandments of God. They set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses; but the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. The Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour, and made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter and in brick and in all manner of service in the field.

The king of Egypt commanded the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill every son born upon the stools and save the daughters alive; but the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. The midwives answered Pharaoh that the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them; the daughters of Israel are not as the women of the nations. Because the midwives feared God, God dealt well with them and made them houses; the Most High blessed the women who saved the children of Israel alive, and the people multiplied and waxed very mighty.
Pharaoh then charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive. ---

Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession and kept back part of the price, his wife being privy to it, and brought only a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet. This continues from Acts 4: none among the believers lacked, because those who possessed lands or houses sold them, laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man as he had need. The church was the epicenter of the community, where counsel was given and economic and community problems were resolved, the way the black Wall Street towns like Rosewood and Tulsa once kept the dollar circulating among our own people for months before it left. A community is a people with all things in common: common government, common heritage, common interest, and common culture, and the word community itself comes from the root "common." So-called black people today are not yet a community, divided by religion, politics, and color, until they come into the fullness of Christ. Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation. -

Peter asks why Satan has filled Ananias' heart to lie to the Holy Ghost and keep back part of the price; while it remained it was his own, so he has not lied unto men but unto the Most High. The spirit upon them was covetousness as well as lying; they saw the full value and coveted it, and did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires. To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy, and to speak every man truth with his neighbour, for we are members one of another. Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform. -

Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost, and the young men wound him up, carried him out, and buried him. This is after the death of Christ, under grace, yet he was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. Grace was never a licence to sin; the wages of sin is death, even now. The christian church hands out a licence to sin by teaching the law is done away and all is covered by grace, and is answerable for the blood in the community when men sin presumptuously believing there are no consequences. Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. -

About three hours later Sapphira came in, not knowing what was done, and agreed to the same lie; Peter told her the feet of those who buried her husband were at the door, and she fell down and yielded up the ghost and was buried by him, and great fear came upon all the church. She shared his fate because they agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Most High. A wife is meant to be a tower against death and a help meet; had she refused the evil or brought it to the leadership, she could have saved his life, as Abigail did. A wife submits to her husband as unto the Most High, in righteousness, not in wickedness; if he tells her to break the law, she is not to agree with him. Not everyone has the same measure of grace; one man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him. -

By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought; they were together in Solomon's porch, believers were the more added, and multitudes brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow them, and they were healed every one. This is the power poured out after they waited in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, fulfilling that these signs would follow them that believe. These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth; they are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim. In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established. -

The high priest and the sect of the Sadducees, filled with indignation, laid hands on the apostles and put them in the common prison, but the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors by night and sent them to stand and speak in the temple all the words of this life. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: what the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse; if you teach this gospel, prison and loss will come, so you cannot be joined to this world. Prepare for it: set aside a nest so your wife and family are provided for if you are locked up, for they will freeze accounts and take houses; the Most High will help, but you must still prepare. Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat. -

At dawn the apostles entered the temple and taught; when the council sent to the prison the officers found it shut with all safety and the keepers standing, but no man within, and word came that the men they had imprisoned were standing in the temple teaching the people. This is boldness: freed from prison, they did not hide but went straight back to teach. If they lock you up, go right back out, the way those who truly love their people keep returning no matter how many times they are jailed.

The captain and officers brought them without violence, fearing the people would stone them, and the high priest charged them, saying, did we not straitly command you not to teach in this name, yet you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine and intend to bring this man's blood upon us. It is the same charge leveled today: that teaching the truth fills the cities with this doctrine and tries to lay guilt on the accusers, the way they say teaching history is only meant to make them feel guilty.

Peter and the apostles answer that we ought to obey the Most High rather than men; the God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom they slew and hanged on a tree, and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses of these things because their lineage experienced his ministry, death, and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it. -

Cut to the heart, the council took counsel to slay them, no different from religious leaders today who take counsel against the truth, publish books against it, and would sooner hire accusers than correct themselves. Then Gamaliel, a Pharisee and a doctor of the law held in reputation among all the people, stood up and commanded the apostles to be put outside a little space. When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High. -

Gamaliel warns the council to take heed what they do: before these days Theudas rose up boasting himself to be somebody, and about four hundred joined him, but he was slain and his followers scattered to nothing; after him Judas of Galilee drew people in the days of the taxing and also perished, and his followers were dispersed. The record of Josephus tells the same of Theudas, a magician who persuaded a great part of the people that he was a prophet who could divide the river Jordan, until horsemen fell on them, killed many, and beheaded him; examine such men and see what their work comes to. Therefore refrain from these men and let them alone: if this counsel or work be of men it will come to nought, but if it be of the Most High it cannot be overthrown, lest they be found to fight against God. Examine our works the same way: if the teaching reforms the brothers off the streets and restores our people's identity worldwide, it is of the Most High; the more they persecute, lock up, and kill, the faster prophecy is filled toward the number to be sealed, so every move is checkmate.

The council agreed with Gamaliel, and when they had called the apostles and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus and let them go. The apostles departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name; that is the level to reach, to rejoice in the beatings, jail, and loss that come with the gospel. Daily in the temple and in every house they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ; this is the pattern, to teach every day on every platform, not once a week. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Be not envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them, for their heart studies destruction and their lips talk of mischief. Through wisdom a house is built, by understanding it is established, and by knowledge the chambers are filled with precious and pleasant riches.

A wise man is strong; a man of knowledge increases strength. By wise counsel you make your war, and in the multitude of counselors there is safety. Something other nations use that black people have not figured out yet starts with an "m": mentorship. People freestyle without a plan and it does not work out. Other nations have mentors who already accomplished what they are trying to do and get counsel, which is advice, on how to reach that level. Some black people are too prideful to ask for help. Wisdom is too high for a fool; he opens not his mouth in the gate.

He that devises to do evil will be called a mischievous person. The thought of foolishness is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to men. The thought of foolishness is sin. We have thoughts we cannot control that pop up, and we have to rebuke them and say that is the devil. All of us have some perverse thoughts, and you have to rebuke them. If you faint in the day of adversity your strength is small.

If you forbear to deliver them that are drawn to death and ready to be slain, and say you knew it not, does not he that ponders the heart consider it and render to every man according to his works? Eat honey because it is good, and the honeycomb which is sweet; so is the knowledge of wisdom to your soul. When you find it there is a reward and your expectation will not be cut off. Cherish knowledge, wisdom, and understanding. Always be in a position to learn and see the lessons in life. Often a regular situation holds a life lesson and you miss it because your antennas are not up.

Lay not wait against the dwelling of the righteous, for a just man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked fall into mischief. Certain brothers come into the truth and make mistakes, but each mistake they learn from and rise up again. He respects brothers who make mistakes and get back in the fight, unlike those too embarrassed to admit they were wrong who run like a little girl. Rejoice not when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles, lest the Most High see it and turn away his wrath from him.

Fret not yourself because of evil men, neither be envious of the wicked, for there is no reward to the evil man and the candle of the wicked will be put out. Whatever the wicked have going on, or riches gotten by wickedness, do not stress over it. The Most High is going to judge them and deal with them, so keep it moving. Fear the Most High and the king, and meddle not with them given to change, for their calamity rises suddenly.

It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. He that says to the wicked, you are righteous, the people will curse and nations abhor him, but to them that rebuke him will be delight and a good blessing. Every man will kiss his lips that gives a right answer.

Prepare your work outside and make it fit in the field, and afterward build your house. Be not a witness against your neighbor without cause, and deceive not with your lips. Say not, I will do to him as he has done to me. This is where turning the other cheek comes from; you have to take the high road instead of getting vengeance. His neighbor drunkenly scratched his car while parking her sister's car, and it took everything in him not to get revenge. He let it go and took the high road.

He went by the field of the slothful and the vineyard of the man void of understanding, and it was all grown over with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down. He considered it well and received instruction: yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep, so your poverty comes as one that travels and your want as an armed man. These chapters deal with wisdom, raising children, avoiding sin, and laziness. These are things we need to put into our character. Proverbs is a very good character-building book that should be read often. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Praise you the Most High. Blessed is the man that feareth the Most High, that delighteth greatly in his commandments. A lot of people try to say they are blessed like the Christians do, saying "I'm blessed, I'm highly favored." But the scripture says blessed is the man that feareth the Most High and delighteth greatly in his commandments. To be blessed you must be keeping the commands and be delighted greatly in them, meaning they are not grievous to you. That is the mindset every single person has to have when it comes to keeping these commandments.
His seed shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed. That is the chosen that get to the kingdom.

Wealth and riches shall be in his house, and his righteousness endureth forever. All the wealth and all the riches will belong to the Israelites when that time comes with Christ to redeem his people. He is going to bring the earth back to the Israelites, and the other nations, the heathens, are going to bring all the wealth back to us. They are going to bring the things that are needed to rebuild the kingdom.
Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness. He is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.
A good man showeth favor and lendeth; he will guide his affairs with discretion.
Surely he shall not be moved forever; the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. -

He shall not be afraid of evil tidings; his heart is fixed, trusting in the Most High. This is the same thing reiterated all through Psalms, how David was not going to be afraid of the things our enemies do against him.
His heart is established; he shall not be afraid, until he see his desire upon his enemies.
He has dispersed, he has given to the poor; his righteousness endureth forever; his horn shall be exalted with honor.
The wicked shall see it and be grieved; he shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away; the desire of the wicked shall perish.
